what_happened: A docs page about the history check was published. It recommended merge commits. The repository's ruleset and decision OP-8 already require squash-only merges and linear history, which Sri had chosen. Nobody read those settings before writing the recommendation, so it had to be withdrawn. No job was attached. This was logged as an intervention and called the writer's own mistake.
cause: Host settings (the ruleset's merge methods and linear-history rule) and owner decisions such as OP-8 live outside the files a writer is given. Nothing makes them an input to docs or advice about the host, and nothing checks such a page against them before it is published. The writer fell back on general practice, where merge commits are a common choice. Athena cannot read the host's merge settings as facts, so the gap shows up only when someone who knows the choice notices.
prevention: Add a host-facts snapshot that Athena fetches and records: allowed merge methods, linear-history and other ruleset rules, and the list of owner decisions that bear on merging. Give the snapshot as required input to any job or hand-written page that makes recommendations about the host. Add a check that fails when such a page recommends a merge method the snapshot disallows or contradicts a listed decision.
proposed_request: Make the repository host's merge settings available to Athena as recorded facts. Athena should read the ruleset (allowed merge methods, linear-history requirement, other protections) and record them in a state file that is refreshed when a job starts. It should give that record, plus the decisions that touch merging (including OP-8), to every job that writes docs or advice about the host. Add a check that fails a docs change when it recommends a merge method the record disallows or contradicts a listed decision. Done when: (1) the record shows squash-only and linear history for this repo; (2) a docs change recommending merge commits fails the check with a message naming the rule; (3) a docs change consistent with the record passes; (4) the history-check page states squash-only and linear history.
